questions.question: The upstream probe's egress (spec §5 Q3, brief §3 invariant 3): (a) broker it — GN7 makes probe.py open every URL through HTTPS_PROXY/SSL_CERT_FILE, refuses before any socket when either is unset, and moves the probe to a system service and timer inside the egress-media namespace as the operator; GN10 declares the media broker instance on core with an allow list of exactly the probe's six hosts and no inject — or (b) record an exception decision naming the probe as operator tooling, withdraw GN7 and drop the probe hosts from GN10's instance?
questions.recommendation: (a) — the standing decision's own words ("The media flake stays brokered"), and invariant 3 has no "deterministic tooling" arm; a user unit outside the namespace could never reach the proxy (the broker drops host-side traffic to it), so the move to system scope is part of brokering it.

questions.question: How far "media absorbed" goes in this batch (spec §5 Q6; charter answers 35, 44, 48): (a) absorb after the media-side work lands — the orchestrator's landing act merges ~/flakes/media as the subtree media/ (branch absorb/media, tag absorbed/media-<rev>, one merge commit), GN11 records it, GN12 moves the flake's outputs into this flake on nixpkgs-host and deletes the inner flake and the media input — or (b) keep the split this increment: GN10's media.url input stays, GN12 is withdrawn, GN11 keeps only the manifest and plan-status tidy-up?
questions.recommendation: (a) — the charter puts "media absorbed" in this increment and PL6 already has the record's row shape; GN12's Step 1 measures whether the ComfyUI closure builds on nixpkgs-host before any move and stops if it does not, so (b) stays available as the fallback.

questions.question: Caddy and the LAN face (spec §3 rows 14c/16b vs decision 20b and the charter's increment 4): (a) wire the worlds with lan.enable = false now — loopback only, no 443, no password files, the feed reached at http://127.0.0.1:<feedPort> and by Helm's link; the LAN face is Isolation's increment-4 task that flips one option and supplies the files — or (b) lan.enable = true in GN10, the operator supplying /var/lib/comfy-secrets/comfy-<w>.users and the two host names before switch #N, with core-media-wiring asserting 443 is the only opened port?
questions.recommendation: (a) — decision 20b and the charter's increment order defer LAN access to Isolation; "Caddy fronts the worlds as designed" is the module as designed, enabled when its inputs exist; (b) adds three operator items and two assertions to GN10.

headings: ### GN1 (code, S) — the feed index: feed.sqlite rebuilt from the PNGs' own chunks, and the worlds' scripts packaged as one directory
### GN2 (code, S) — the job queue: enqueue with a seed, submit to ComfyUI, poll, never raise on the network
### GN3 (code, M) — the feed replaces the placeholder: a vertical page of the newest renders, forms only, zero outbound
### GN4 (code, S) — the three verbs: like, regenerate with a new seed, edit the prompt — each a form POST into the queue
### GN5 (code, S) — the rules mutator: a mutation grammar read from the lab's manifest, applied to a graph, deterministic under a seed
### GN6 (code, S) — comfy-mutate: the world-aware command, its wrapper and the on-demand user unit
### GN7 (code, S) — the upstream probe goes through the broker: a proxied opener that refuses before any socket, and the unit moved inside the media namespace
### GN8 (code, S) — engagement: the feed counts opens, dwell and likes per UTC day and POSTs them to Helm's loopback endpoint
### GN9 (docs, S) — the runbook and the acceptance drill carry the feed, the verbs, the mutator and the brokered probe
### GN10 (code, M) — the worlds on core: the media input, the media broker instance, the on-demand units, the backup paths and the wiring check
### GN11 (code, S) — the absorption's record: the GN row owns media/, the media repo row, the plan-status rows and the untyped record file
### GN12 (code, M) — media absorbed into this flake: the outputs move onto nixpkgs-host, the inner flake and the input go
